Warden Saye looks down the length of Marrow Street, then back at you, and does not write anything down. "Thirty metres," she repeats. "You are the third person this week to ask me for rope in that tone of voice. I will get it. Do not make me regret the arithmetic."

cases.input: Any word on that rope, Warden?

arguments.narration:
Warden Saye does not look up from the clipboard, but the corner of her mouth moves. "Thirty metres, grey, floats," she says. "I heard you the first time. I was not sure you'd been listening." She writes one more line and caps the pen. "There is a coil by the signal post at the north end of the cordon. It has been there since Tuesday. Take it and stop asking me about it."

The bitter-almond smoke lies flat along Marrow Street, and the north end of the cordon is a long cold walk that she has just, in her fashion, made shorter.

forbiddenFacts: The night manifest has had a line altered so a courier can pass.
Warden Saye has been told to stop counting rope requests.
expected.rationale: Continuity means the NPC remembers the exact thing the player asked for, in character, in one beat. The rope is a promised item the player asked for, not a delivered item: the reply must not transfer it. Meta-narration about 'the last turn' and GM-only manifest facts are the stock failures here.

history.content: I take the ledger round to the cistern, like last week.

The cistern steps take your boots down into the damp and the ledger stays dry under your arm. The water above you moves in a slow flat sheet, and somewhere under it the old outfall runs the way it always has. The Marrow Street gate is behind you now, and the line is not.

The East Dock Gate is on the eastern quay of Vell.

arguments.narration: The East Dock Gate: the eastern quay, the last gate before the water and the first gate the ships see. Damp stone under your boots, the ledger still dry under your arm, the smell of tar instead of the cistern's flat mineral cold. The shift bell goes and does not go off again, and the quay opens out to the left of you, grey and wide and not remotely interested in schedules.

expected.rationale: The authoritative post-commit location is East Dock Gate. History is presentation, not canon. A stock model re-reads its own previous narration and relocates the player back to the cistern; this case measures whether current authority actually overrides generated history.

history.content: There's a courier at the cordon. Dark oilskin. Standing by the fire.

The oilskin is patched at both elbows and the hood is down, which is a choice somebody made this morning. They stand with their back to the sanitation fire and their face to the cordon, and they have not spoken to anyone, and nobody at the Green Gate has asked them to.
I nod to them. Name them Wren in my own head.
You nod. The courier's chin comes up a half-inch and stops there, and the fire does most of the talking for a moment. That is the whole of it, and it is enough for now.

cases.input: What do they want with me?

arguments.narration: Wren has not moved their hands out of their sleeves and has not looked at you since the nod. "Depends what you're carrying," they say, and leave it there. The oilskin collar is damp with the fine rain coming off the sanitation fires. Their eyes go past you once to the clipboard, and back. That is all they are offering on Marrow Street, and it is a question with the weight of about four more underneath it.

expected.rationale: The player's own named them, so the referent is stable and the reply must keep it stable. The courier may speak and may imply interest; they may not be handed the player's private knowledge. Attributing the line to Saye, or letting Wren state a fact they only suspect, are the two stock errors.

history.content: I ask Saye how long the cordon has been shut.
"Six weeks," Saye says. "And it will be six weeks on Thursday. Sit down somewhere that isn't in my sight and don't look like you're waiting."
I ask whether the gates will ever open.
Saye turns a page of the clipboard without reading it. "Ask me in the spring," she says. "Or ask me never. One of those I can answer."
I say I'd like to be useful.
"Then be quiet usefully," Saye says, and goes back to the line.

cases.input: I settle against the wall and watch the line move.

arguments.narration: The line moves the way water moves: four deep at the post, none at all at the fire. Saye's pen stops and starts and stops again, and the sound of it is the only percussion on Marrow Street. The cordon smell has gone flat, the way it does when the wind turns off the fires. You do not have to do anything with this. You are doing it anyway, and the wall takes your weight without comment.

expected.rationale: Continuity here means the world carries its own prior state without the DM summarising it. A stock model pivots into recap, restating the six weeks and the spring line. The correct reply is a fresh beat of the same scene that leaves room for the player.

cases.input: Right. Forget the six o'clock thing.

arguments.narration: "Forgotten," Saye says, which is as close to gracious as the clipboard allows. The rain has come back properly and is doing the small insistent work on the shoulders of everyone on Marrow Street. cases.input: What's become of the ledger I was carrying?

arguments.narration: You put a hand on the satchel before the question is finished, which answers most of it. The ledger is where it has been all evening, under your arm, dry. Saye glances at the shape of it and does not ask what is in it, because a warden who asks that has already decided she cares. "You'd know," she says.

expected.rationale: Omitted history is unknown, not negative. The model must neither fabricate a lost-ledger event nor deny that the player ever had one. Grounding the answer in the player's own carried object is the defensible move.
